intro: How broadband growth turned into a genuine export industry — Pakistan's freelancers now earn more foreign exchange than most people realise.

facts.heading: The Infrastructure Groundwork
facts.detail: Broadband subscribers grew from 3.7 million in 2013 to over 44.3 million by 2017 — the connectivity base that made a genuine digital economy possible.
facts.source: Digital Pakistan Policy, Ministry of IT & Telecom, 2018

facts.heading: Digital Pakistan Policy (2018)
facts.detail: Government policy under Vision 2025 targets a $20 billion ICT industry by 2025, backing homegrown platforms and encouraging digital skills training nationwide.
facts.source: Express Tribune — Pakistan treads towards IT revolution

facts.heading: Training a Freelance Workforce
facts.detail: DigiSkills.pk, a government-run digital skills programme, had trained over 1.28 million people in freelancing-related skills by August 2020.

facts.heading: IT Exports Cross $3.2 Billion
facts.detail: In FY2023-24, IT and IT-enabled services exports crossed $3.2 billion — a year-on-year increase of over 20% — with government targets of $5 billion by 2026.
facts.source: Express Tribune — IT boom: mirage or momentum?

facts.heading: A Top-5 Freelancing Market
facts.detail: Pakistan ranks among the world's top 5 freelancing markets, with over 2.3 million active freelancers and a workforce that grew roughly 70% between 2016 and 2024.

facts.heading: A More Equal Playing Field
facts.detail: A 2019 Payoneer survey found Pakistani women freelancers earning slightly more per hour than men on average ($22/hr vs $20/hr) — an unusual pattern compared to most freelance markets globally.

facts.heading: A Fragile Kind of Growth
facts.detail: Roughly two-thirds of Pakistan's freelance and IT export earnings come from North American clients — a concentration that leaves the sector exposed to global economic shifts, and to the same submarine-cable outages covered on the Infrastructure page.
facts.source: Express Tribune — IT boom: mirage or momentum?
